canonical_title: Mission closure explicitly retains known non-blocking follow-ups instead of treating acceptance as resolving them
summary: Despite reaching disposition CLOSED — ACCEPTED, SB-OPS-CI-ARCHITECTURE-1.0's closure records explicitly list non-blocking follow-up items and state they are not represented as resolved by the closure. The exact follow-up list was not perfectly stable between the pre-merge acceptance record and the final post-merge closure record, which is itself a limitation worth surfacing rather than eliding.

claims.text: At pre-merge acceptance, Mission Control listed five non-blocking findings carried forward as follow-up items outside the mission, explicitly stating 'None is silently resolved by this acceptance.'

evidence.locator: ## 4. Non-blocking findings carried forward: five-item list plus 'None is silently resolved by this acceptance.'

claims.text: At final post-merge closure, Mission Control again explicitly listed four carried follow-ups (transient Auth/JWKS-class flakiness; GitHub Actions runtime deprecation warning; existing dependency vulnerability backlog; pre-existing inventory shared-write-path diagnostic) and stated they 'remain outside this mission's closure and are not represented as resolved.'

evidence.locator: ## Carried follow-ups: four-item list plus 'remain outside this mission's closure and are not represented as resolved'
## Final Reconciled Closure, follow-up sentence naming the same four items as unresolved and non-blocking

claims.text: The pre-merge acceptance record's five-item follow-up list included a future branch-protection policy decision for Fast Gate; the final post-merge closure record and the archive manifest both name only four items and do not mention the branch-protection item, without stating whether it was resolved, superseded, or simply dropped. This inconsistency is itself a genuine limitation of the closure evidence, not a resolved fact.

evidence.locator: ## 4. Non-blocking findings carried forward, fifth bullet: 'future branch-protection policy decision for Fast Gate, if Founder/Mission Control later chooses to require it'
## Carried follow-ups: four-item list with no branch-protection item and no statement addressing its omission

conditions: Applies to any mission closure that carries forward known non-blocking issues rather than requiring full resolution before acceptance.
anti_patterns: Treating a CLOSED / ACCEPTED disposition as an implicit signal that all previously identified issues are resolved.
Narrowing a follow-up list between successive closure records without an explicit note explaining why an item was dropped.
